title: Finite reductions of Verdier duality
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $1\le m\le n$ and let $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\to B=A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ be the quotient map. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the bounded constructible finite-Tor category $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with the corresponding étale constructibility convention [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Put $K_B=K\otimes_A^LB$ using derived scalar extension on that site [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. On the étale site put $\omega_{X,A}=Ra_{X,A}^{\times}A$, where $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the structure morphism, and $D_{X,A}K=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,\omega_{X,A})$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, lem-weil-duality-pairing]; define $\omega_{X,B}$ and $D_{X,B}$ similarly. On the finite-coefficient pro-étale constructible category use the dualizing object transported by the site comparison [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison]. On either finite coefficient site, for every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$
d_{K,A,B}:(D_{X,A}K)\otimes_A^LB\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,B}(K_B).
$$
The maps form a cocycle under further coefficient quotients and carry evaluation and the double-dual morphism to the corresponding maps at $B$. If $\dim X\le d$ and $K$ has Tor interval $[a,b]$, both sides have Tor interval $[-b-2d,-a]$. Here Tor interval $[a,b]$ means that $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^LN)=0$ for every $i\notin[a,b]$ and every sheaf $N$ of $A$-modules in degree zero, on the site under consideration.

proof.text:
First work on the étale site. The constant sheaf $A_X$ is constructible with Tor interval $[0,0]$: tensoring with the free rank-one coefficient sheaf is the identity, so this is the definition [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. By the Hom-complex definition [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $R\mathcal Hom_A(A_X,\omega_{X,A})=\omega_{X,A}$ (the Hom complex from the degree-zero unit to a K-injective representative is that representative). Apply [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] to $A_X$ to obtain $\omega_{X,A}\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{Et}},A)$. The same result applied to $K$ gives $D_{X,A}K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{Et}},A)$; this also permits applying the eventual comparison to $D_{X,A}K$.

We also check that the reduced inputs used in the cocycle remain in the required category. For any $T\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{Et}},A)$ with Tor interval $[h,j]$, the constructible variant of [lem-sf-flat-model] gives a bounded flat constructible model $P$ in $[h,j]$ (its finite-type-over-$k$ hypothesis applies to $X$). A bounded flat complex is K-flat: tensor with an acyclic complex and filter the total complex by the finitely many degrees of $P$; each successive quotient is acyclic by flatness. Thus, since derived change of rings is computed on K-flat complexes [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] (2), $T_B$ is represented by $P\otimes_A B$. On every stratum trivializing $P^i$, its coefficient extension is the constant finite $B$-module $P^i_{\bar x}\otimes_A B$, so each term is constructible. The kernel and cokernel clauses of [thm-constructible-serre], applied to its differentials, make its cohomology constructible. Each term is $B$-flat because $(P^i\otimes_A B)\otimes_B N=P^i\otimes_A N$ and restriction of $B$-module sheaves to $A$-module sheaves is exact. The same finite filtration proves $P\otimes_A B$ K-flat; tensoring it with a degree-zero $B$-module sheaf has terms only in $[h,j]$. Consequently $T_B\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{Et}},B)$ with that interval. Apply this to $T=K,\omega_{X,A},D_AK$, and repeat for $B\to C$ when needed below.

source.place: Proof, prerequisite for applying thm-coef-finite-hom with second argument omega_{X,A}

proof.text:
By [thm-coef-finite-hom], with its second argument $\omega_{X,A}$ now verified finite-Tor constructible, the evaluation-defined map $v_{K,\omega_A}$ is an isomorphism. Let $u:\omega_{X,A}\otimes_A^LB\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,B}$ be [lem-coef-finite-dualizing]. Define
$$d_{K,A,B}=R\mathcal Hom_B(K_B,u)\circ v_{K,\omega_A}.$$
Both factors are isomorphisms; the second-variable functor in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] takes an isomorphism to an isomorphism. This proves the displayed isomorphism. Naturality of evaluation-defined $v$ in $K$, postcomposition by the fixed $u$, and functoriality of internal Hom make $d$ natural (contravariantly) in $K$.

source.place: Proof, first two sentences: construct d by v then u

proof.text:
Write $S=-\otimes_A^LB$. Its tensor identifications preserve associativity and evaluation by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; the general internal-Hom comparison respects evaluation by [thm-coef-finite-hom]. Consequently the definition of $d$ gives the actual equality of pairings
$$\operatorname{ev}_{K_B}\circ(d_{K,A,B}\otimes_B^L1_{K_B})=u\circ S(\operatorname{ev}_K),$$
where $S(D_AK\otimes_A^LK)$ is identified with $S(D_AK)\otimes_B^LK_B$. Indeed the evaluation identity for $v$ has right side $S(\operatorname{ev}_K)$ with target $S\omega_A$; composing with $u$ and using naturality of evaluation in its target gives precisely this equation. The evaluation maps are those of [lem-weil-duality-pairing], and the chosen $u$ is the counit-compatible comparison of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing].

The double-dual map $\delta_K$ is the transpose of evaluation with tensor symmetry by [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. Under the tensor--Hom adjunction, which [thm-coef-finite-hom] respects, both arrows in
$$d_{D_AK,A,B}\circ S(\delta_K)=D_B(d_{K,A,B})\circ\delta_{K_B}$$
have source $K_B$ and target $D_B(S(D_AK))$. To compute the left transpose, apply Step 3 with input $D_AK$, then precompose with $S(\delta_K)\otimes1$. This gives $u\circ S(\operatorname{ev}_{D_AK}\circ(\delta_K\otimes1_{D_AK}))$. The definition of $\delta_K$ as the evaluation transpose says exactly that $\operatorname{ev}_{D_AK}\circ(\delta_K\otimes1)=\operatorname{ev}_K\circ\tau_{K,D_AK}$, where $\tau$ is tensor symmetry. For the right transpose, precomposition in internal Hom is adjoint to precomposition in its tensor argument. Hence transposing $D_B(d_K)\circ\delta_{K_B}$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_{D_BK_B}\circ(\delta_{K_B}\otimes d_K)$, which by the same defining equation for $\delta_{K_B}$ equals $\operatorname{ev}_{K_B}\circ(d_K\otimes1)\circ\tau_{K_B,S(D_AK)}$. Step 3 with input $K$ equates these transposes; injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the equation. Here $D_AK$ is in the required domain by Step 1. Since $d_K$ is an isomorphism, this equation is exactly compatibility with double duals after identifying $S(D_A^2K)$ with $D_B^2(K_B)$ using $D_B(d_K)^{-1}\circ d_{D_AK}$. On K-flat models scalar change is termwise tensor with $B$ placed in degree zero: on homogeneous tensors of degrees $i,j$, symmetry is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$ both before and after scalar change. Thus the symmetry used in these two transposes has the same sign.

source.place: Proof, transposing evaluation gives double-dual compatibility

proof.text:
For $A=A_{E,n}\to B=A_{E,m}\to C=A_{E,r}$, $1\le r\le m$, identify $S_{B,C}S_{A,B}$ with $S_{A,C}$ by the tensor comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Expand $d$ as $R\mathcal Hom(-,u)\circ v$. Successive-change compatibility of $v$ in [thm-coef-finite-hom] and its naturality in the second argument collect the two Hom factors into $R\mathcal Hom_C(K_C,u_{B,C}\circ S_{B,C}u_{A,B})$. The quotient cocycle in [lem-coef-finite-dualizing] identifies this last argument map with $u_{A,C}$. Thus
$$d_{K,A,C}=d_{K_B,B,C}\circ S_{B,C}(d_{K,A,B}).$$
For an identity quotient the evaluation transpose and the dualizing counit transpose are identities, so this includes the identity part of the cocycle.

If $\dim X\le d$ and $K$ has Tor interval $[a,b]$, [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] gives interval $[-b-2d,-a]$ for $D_AK$. For every $B$-module sheaf $N$ in degree zero, take a K-flat representative $P$ with flat terms for $D_AK$. Such a representative and its scalar extension being K-flat are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] for the identity topos with coefficient map $A_X\to B_X$. Then
$$(P\otimes_A B)\otimes_B N\longrightarrow P\otimes_A N,\quad (p\otimes b)\otimes z\longmapsto p\otimes bz$$
is a chain isomorphism, inverse $p\otimes z\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes z$. It identifies $S(D_AK)\otimes_B^LN$ with $D_AK\otimes_A^LN$, which vanishes outside $[-b-2d,-a]$ by the definition [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Hence the left side of $d$ has the claimed Tor interval; its isomorphism to the right side gives the same interval there. No flatness of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Proof, Tor bound and preservation of Tor interval by scalar extension

proof.text:
For a pro-étale input, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] gives $K\cong
u_X^*K'$ for an étale bounded constructible $K'$. By [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] (ii), $K'$ has the same Tor interval and is an allowed input above. Constant coefficient sheaves are preserved by $
u_X^*$: the constant sheaf of a set is the coproduct of copies of the terminal sheaf, and an inverse-image functor preserves coproducts and finite limits, including the ring operations on these sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $
u_X$ with constant coefficient $A$. Its tensor comparison with the constant $A$-module $B$ gives the $B$-linear identification $
u_X^*(T\otimes_A^LB)\cong
u_X^*T\otimes_A^LB$.

The dualizing and internal-Hom comparisons of [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison], with second argument $\omega_{X,A}$ verified by Step 1, identify $
u_X^*D_AK'$ with $D_A(
u_X^*K')$ and identify evaluations and double-dual maps. Define $u_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by pulling back the étale isomorphism $u$ of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing] and composing the just-specified tensor and dualizing identifications. Its quotient cocycle follows by pulling back the étale cocycle: the tensor identifications are the balanced tensor maps, and both reassociations send $(p\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $p\otimes bc$. This uses the transported dualizing object; it requires no ambient pro-étale exceptional adjunction.

The map $v$ of [thm-coef-finite-hom] on the pro-étale site is defined by transposing evaluation. Its second argument $\omega_{X,A,\mathrm{proet}}\cong
u_X^*\omega_{X,A}$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] (i) applied to Step 1, so that theorem applies there. Since the site comparisons identify evaluation, uniqueness of its transpose identifies the pullback of $d_{K',A,B}$ with $R\mathcal Hom_B(K_B,u_{\mathrm{proet}})\circ v_{K,\omega_A}$. This constructs the natural pro-étale isomorphism. Steps 3--4 apply to this composite using the same evaluation identities, and its cocycle is the pulled-back cocycle just checked. Step 1 gives the bounded constructible reduced étale objects; their pullbacks are bounded constructible by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. Finally the Tor interval for the étale $D_AK'$ is carried unchanged to its pro-étale dual by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] (i) and the duality identification. Step 6's balanced-tensor calculation on the pro-étale site preserves this interval under coefficient reduction, so both sides have $[-b-2d,-a]$.

split_report.summary: Bound the implicit quotient levels, coefficient category and scheme hypotheses faithfully to the source; verified the dualizing object is an allowed second argument; gave seven steps with explicit evaluation, double-dual and cocycle equations, a K-flat Tor calculation, and separate finite-site transport. No new nodes. Second reading explicitly verified reduced-input constructibility, expanded the double-dual transpose calculation, and defined the pro-étale dualizing comparison by transport.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1--2 realize the first two source sentences (Hom comparison with omega then dualizing comparison). Steps 3--4 expand evaluation and transposed double-dual compatibility. Step 5 expands the quotient cocycle. Step 6 proves the last Tor-bound sentence by an explicit balanced-tensor chain map. Step 7 makes the finite pro-étale realization explicit, following the source proofs of the two coefficient-comparison inputs.

tool_uses.why: Independent étale Verdier preservation and its Tor bound; this is exactly the bound cited by the blueprint proof and verifies the Hom-comparison domain.
Generic finite-quotient tensor and associator coherence, not a replacement for general Hom comparison; needed to type the evaluation and quotient equations.

Generic K-flat change-of-rings tool: its identity-topos specialization says a flat-term K-flat resolution remains K-flat after scalar extension. No own-unit statement supplies that resolution property.
Generic finite coefficient site-comparison equivalence, used only to obtain an étale representative of a pro-étale input.
Generic preservation and detection of the Tor interval under finite-site comparison; needed to verify the representative hypothesis and transport the bound.
Generic identification of dualizing objects, Hom, evaluation and double-dual maps on the two sites; needed for the finite pro-étale realization, as in the source input proofs.
Generic bounded flat constructible resolution on the etale site; verifies that every reduced input remains finite-Tor constructible before the cocycle is applied.
Generic kernel and cokernel closure for finite-ring constructible sheaves; applies to the bounded coefficient-extended model and proves constructibility of its cohomology.
